title_en: Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin v. Bei Hongfeng, Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending
ruling_gist_en: Article 125 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'Where the parties dispute the understanding of a clause in a contract, the true meaning of the clause shall be determined in accordance with the wording used in the contract, the relevant provisions of the contract, the purpose of the contract, trade practices, and the principle of good faith.' The contract signed by the parties is a 'Guaranteed Loan Contract'. Specifically, the purpose of the first paragraph of Article 4 of this contract is to ensure the lender's right to know and supervise the use of the funds, so that when the lender discovers that the borrower has changed the purpose of the funds without authorization or other situations that may affect the lender's rights, the lender can take timely measures to recover the funds and interest. Using the principles of teleological interpretation, it can be understood that providing false materials and reports will indeed affect the lender's supervision over the borrower's use of the funds, but failing to provide relevant materials and reports will prevent the lender from understanding the use of the funds involved in the case, which is detrimental to the timely exercise of its rights. Therefore, the borrower's failure to provide relevant materials and reports to the lender for more than two years after borrowing constitutes a breach of contract.

full_text_en:
Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin v. Bei Hongfeng, Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over private lending

【Ruling Summary】

Article 125 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where the parties dispute the understanding of a contract clause, the true meaning of that clause shall be determined according to the words and expressions used in the contract, the relevant clauses of the contract, the purpose of the contract, trade practices, and the principle of good faith." The contract signed by the parties was a Guaranteed Loan Contract. Specifically, the purpose of the first paragraph of Article 4 of that contract was to ensure the lender's right to be informed and to supervise the use of the funds, so that the lender could take timely measures to recover the funds and interest upon discovering that the borrower had unilaterally changed the use of the funds or other circumstances that might affect the lender's rights. Applying the principle of purposive interpretation, it can be understood that providing untrue materials and statements would certainly affect the lender's supervision over the borrower's use of funds, but failing to provide relevant materials and statements would prevent the lender from learning about the use of the funds in question, which would be detrimental to the lender's timely exercise of its rights. Therefore, the borrower's failure to provide relevant materials and statements to the lender for more than two years during the loan period constitutes a breach of contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2014) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 38

Appellant (Original Defendant): Bei Hongfeng, male, Manchu ethnicity, born on October 21, 1964, supervisor of Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd., residing in Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Sun Wenbing, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 7, 1966, manager of Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Guo Shun, lawyer of Heilongjiang Baicheng Law Firm.

Appellant (Original Defendant): Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Shuangtaizi Village, Shuangtaizi Township, Faku County, Shenyang City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xicai, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Sun Wenbing, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 7, 1966, manager of Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Guo Shun, lawyer of Heilongjiang Baicheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Li Zhanjiang, male, Han ethnicity, born on November 22, 1972, Chairman of the Board of Yichun Hongjiang Industrial Co., Ltd., residing in Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Gao Ming, lawyer of Beijing Huacheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongmei, lawyer of Heilongjiang Xinfei Law Firm.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Zhu Limin, female, Han ethnicity, born on December 10, 1964, Chairman of the Board of Shenyang Delicheng Commercial Trade Co., Ltd., residing in Yichun City, Heilongjiang Province.

Agent ad litem: Gao Ming, lawyer of Beijing Huacheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongmei, lawyer of Heilongjiang Xinfei Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over private lending between the appellants Bei Hongfeng and Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Donghao Company) and the respondents Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, the Heilongjiang Higher People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Heilongjiang High Court) rendered the Civil Judgment (2013) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9 on December 10, 2013. Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court legally formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on March 4, 2014. Bei Hongfeng and his agents ad litem Sun Wenbing and Guo Shun, the agent ad litem of Donghao Company, Sun Wenbing and Guo Shun, and the common agents ad litem of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, Gao Ming and Jiang Hongmei, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case has now been concluded.

The facts found by the first-instance court: On December 14, 2009, Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin, Bei Hongfeng, and Donghao Company signed a Guaranteed Loan Contract, mainly stipulating: Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin would lend RMB 70 million to Bei Hongfeng; the purpose of the loan was to operate the "University Classic" real estate project developed by Donghao Company; the loan term was from December 15, 2009 to June 15, 2010; Bei Hongfeng was required to provide relevant statements and materials to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin; if Bei Hongfeng failed to repay on time, provided untrue statements and materials, or committed other acts of default, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to stop the loan and demand early repayment of the principal already lent; Donghao Company would provide joint and several liability guarantee for Bei Hongfeng with all its own assets and projects under construction, the scope of guarantee including but not limited to the principal debt, interest (penalty interest), liquidated damages, litigation costs, travel expenses, lawyer fees, and all other expenses for realizing the claim. On the same day the contract was signed, Li Zhanjiang remitted RMB 20 million to Bei Hongfeng, and Zhu Limin remitted RMB 20 million to Donghao Company through a third party, Shenyang Delicheng Commercial Trade Co., Ltd. Bei Hongfeng issued a receipt and a promissory note to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin. The receipt stated: "Received RMB 15 million each from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin." Bei Hongfeng signed at the end. The promissory note stated: "Borrowed RMB 70 million from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin (Shenyang Delicheng Commercial Trade Co., Ltd.) (see loan agreement), borrower: Bei Hongfeng."

In October 2011, Bei Hongfeng transferred 40% of his equity in Donghao Company to a third party, Zhu Libing, as a mortgage guarantee for the debt in question, and completed the change of shareholder registration at the industry and commerce authority. After the change, the shareholding ratio of Donghao Company was: Bei Hongfeng held 50%, Zhu Libing held 40%, and Zhang Xicai held 10%.

On April 14, 2012, Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin, Bei Hongfeng, and Donghao Company signed another Guaranteed Loan Contract Supplementary Agreement (I) (hereinafter referred to as the Supplementary Agreement), mainly stipulating: Bei Hongfeng borrowed RMB 70 million from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin on December 14, 2009 due to project needs, with Donghao Company providing joint and several liability guarantee. The aforementioned principal of RMB 70 million and interest had not been repaid; Bei Hongfeng had mortgaged 40% of Donghao Company's equity to Zhu Libing, the designated agent of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, on October 14, 2011; as of April 14, 2012, the reduced interest amount payable by Bei Hongfeng under the Guaranteed Loan Contract was RMB 40 million, and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin waived other interest and liquidated damages; Bei Hongfeng promised to repay all principal and interest by September 30, 2012; the interest on the loan from April 15, 2012 to September 14, 2012 would be calculated at RMB 700,000 per month; if Bei Hongfeng failed to repay the principal and interest before September 14, 2012, from September 15 onward, Bei Hongfeng would pay interest at RMB 1.05 million per month; if Bei Hongfeng delayed repayment, he should bear the costs incurred by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin to realize their claims, including lawyer agency fees, travel expenses, etc.; Donghao Company would continue to act as Bei Hongfeng's guarantor, assuming joint and several liability for all debts under the supplementary agreement, with the guarantee period lasting until all debts were fully repaid. Bei Hongfeng signed at the borrower's section, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin signed at the lender's section, and Donghao Company affixed its company seal and the seal of its legal representative and shareholder Zhang Xicai at the guarantor's section. On the same day, Donghao Company held a shareholders' meeting regarding the guarantee for Bei Hongfeng's borrowing from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, and adopted a resolution: agreeing that Donghao Company would provide joint and several liability guarantee for Bei Hongfeng's borrowing of RMB 70 million from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin; agreeing to all contents of the Guaranteed Loan Contract and the Supplementary Agreement. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law), Bei Hongfeng recused himself from this shareholders' meeting, and Zhu Libing signed at the shareholder signature section.

On July 4, 2012, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin signed a Entrusted Agency Agreement with Beijing Huacheng Law Firm (hereinafter referred to as Huacheng Law Firm). Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin entrusted Huacheng Law Firm as their litigation agent in the private lending dispute with Bei Hongfeng et al., and agreed that the fee method would be a contingency fee, with payment due seven days after the court's judgment. On June 24, 2013, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin signed another Agency Supplementary Agreement with Huacheng Law Firm, changing the fee method from contingency to a percentage of the subject amount, and changing the payment time from after the court's judgment to phased payment: an upfront agency fee of RMB 3.3 million, payable 30 days before the first-instance court hearing; a later agency fee of 5% of the realized claim amount, payable within 7 days after realization of the claim; and a unified fee receipt would be issued after case closure. On July 5, 2013, a third party, Yichun Zhongrun Investment Co., Ltd., remitted RMB 3.3 million to Huacheng Law Firm and issued a certificate confirming that it paid the aforementioned agency fee of RMB 3.3 million on behalf of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin. Huacheng Law Firm issued a payment receipt to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin on July 8 of the same year.

The first-instance court also found that, according to the relevant provisions of the Fee Guidelines, the fee standard for Beijing law firms representing parties in civil litigation on a percentage of the subject amount is: 10% for amounts up to RMB 100,000 (including RMB 100,000); 6% for amounts from RMB 100,000 to RMB 1 million (including RMB 1 million); 4% for amounts from RMB 1 million to RMB 10 million (including RMB 10 million); 2% for amounts above RMB 10 million, calculated on a progressive differential basis based on the disputed amount. Law firms may also negotiate with the parties to charge agency fees higher than the aforementioned guidelines.

The first-instance court further found that during the performance of the contract, Bei Hongfeng failed to provide the relevant statements and materials to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin as required by the Guaranteed Loan Contract.

On July 16, 2012, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed a lawsuit against Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company as defendants in the Yichun Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province (hereinafter referred to as Yichun Intermediate Court). After accepting the case, based on the property preservation application of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, the court successively made civil rulings (2012) Yi Zhong Min Chu Zi Nos. 1-1, 1-2, 1-3, and 1-5, sealing up Bei Hongfeng's 50% equity in Donghao Company, as well as Donghao Company's land use rights and construction in progress. On July 19, 2012, Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company raised a jurisdictional objection; after review, the Heilongjiang High Court ruled that the case should be transferred from Yichun Intermediate Court.

Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin alleged that on December 14, 2009, they, together with Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company, signed a Guaranteed Loan Contract, stipulating: Bei Hongfeng borrowed RMB 70 million from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin for the development of the "University Classic" real estate project in Huanggu District, Shenyang City, with a term from December 15, 2009 to June 15, 2010. Donghao Company assumed joint and several payment liability for the aforementioned loan, the scope of guarantee including the principal debt, interest (penalty interest), liquidated damages, litigation costs, travel expenses, lawyer fees, and all other expenses for realizing the claim. After the contract was signed, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin performed their obligations in accordance with the contract. On April 14, 2012, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin signed a Supplementary Agreement with Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company, partially reducing the interest payable by Bei Hongfeng. However, Bei Hongfeng violated the Guaranteed Loan Contract and the Supplementary Agreement by refusing to provide statements and materials, failing to disclose the use of the loan and the existence of disputes with third parties, and even concealing and transferring property at low prices to outsiders. Therefore, they prayed the court to order: 1. Bei Hongfeng to immediately repay the loan of RMB 70 million; 2. Bei Hongfeng to immediately pay loan interest (interest of RMB 40 million up to April 2012; interest of RMB 700,000 per month from April 15, 2012 to September 14, 2012; and interest of RMB 1.05 million per month from September 15, 2012 to the date of actual payment) and the lawyer fees of RMB 3.3 million incurred due to litigation; 3. Donghao Company to assume joint and several liability for the aforementioned debts; 4. Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Bei Hongfeng argued: 1. The term of the loan had not yet expired; Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had no right to sue for early repayment, and their claims should be dismissed; 2. The actual principal of the loan was not RMB 70 million but RMB 40 million; the remaining RMB 30 million was interest included in the principal; therefore, interest should be calculated based on a principal of RMB 40 million; 3. Because Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit early and sealed up Donghao Company's properties for sale, Bei Hongfeng was unable to repay the loan; thus, the default should not be attributed to Bei Hongfeng; 4. Since Bei Hongfeng did not breach the contract and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin failed to provide a formal invoice from Huacheng Law Firm, indicating that the fee had not actually been incurred, Bei Hongfeng should not bear the lawyer fees paid by the other party.

Donghao Company argued: 1. It agreed with Bei Hongfeng's defense; 2. Because a company cannot provide a guarantee for its shareholder, the guarantee in question was invalid; moreover, even if the guarantee were valid, since the loan term had not expired, the guarantor should not bear guarantee liability; 3. Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin should compensate Donghao Company for the losses caused by the early property preservation.

The first-instance court held that the Guaranteed Loan Contract and its Supplementary Agreement were the true expressions of the parties' intentions, and their contents did not violate any mandatory provisions regarding validity under laws and administrative regulations, and thus should be deemed lawful and valid. The three focal issues in dispute in this case were as follows:

1. Whether Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to demand early repayment of the loan from Bei Hongfeng. According to the Guaranteed Loan Contract, when Bei Hongfeng failed to repay on time, provided untrue statements and materials, or committed other acts of default, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to stop the loan and demand early repayment of the principal lent. During the performance of the contract, Bei Hongfeng did not provide statements and related materials as agreed, which constituted a breach of contract and satisfied the conditions for demanding early repayment as agreed by both parties. Therefore, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to demand early repayment from Bei Hongfeng in accordance with the contract. The application for property preservation by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin was a lawful exercise of their litigation rights, and there was no evidence to prove that the sealing had caused losses to Bei Hongfeng or Donghao Company; therefore, this property preservation did not affect Bei Hongfeng's obligation to repay.

2. How to determine the principal and interest amounts under the loan contract. Although the Guaranteed Loan Contract, the Supplementary Agreement, and the receipt issued by Bei Hongfeng to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin all recorded the loan principal as RMB 70 million, based on the amount actually paid by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin and their admission in court, the actual loan principal was RMB 40 million. Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin claimed that the remaining RMB 30 million was compensation promised by Bei Hongfeng, but they failed to provide evidence to support this claim. Moreover, both parties were aware that the loan was for commercial purposes, yet they did not agree on interest during the loan period, which was contrary to common sense; Bei Hongfeng's claim that the RMB 30 million was interest was more credible. Therefore, the first-instance court confirmed that the RMB 30 million was interest, and the loan principal should be confirmed as RMB 40 million. According to the Supplementary Agreement, the parties' agreement on the amount or calculation standard of interest was divided into three stages: the first stage from December 15, 2009 to April 14, 2012, with an interest amount of RMB 40 million; the second stage from April 15, 2012 to September 14, 2012, with interest calculated at RMB 700,000 per month; the third stage from September 15, 2012 to the date of actual payment, with interest calculated at RMB 1.05 million per month. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Lending Cases, which provides that "the interest rate for private lending may be appropriately higher than the bank interest rate, and local people's courts may flexibly grasp according to the actual circumstances of their region, but the maximum shall not exceed four times the interest rate of similar loans from banks; if this limit is exceeded, the interest on the excess portion shall not be protected," the calculation of interest for the first and third stages exceeded the standard set by this judicial interpretation, so the excess portion was not protected. During those periods, interest should be calculated based on four times the bank lending rate for similar loans. The interest calculation for the second stage complied with this judicial interpretation, so interest for that period could be calculated according to the standard agreed by the parties. Based on the aforementioned calculation method, with a principal of RMB 40 million, from December 15, 2009 to December 10, 2013 (the date of the first-instance judgment), calculated in stages based on four times the benchmark lending rate for loans with a term of three to five years as published by the People's Bank of China, the interest on the loan in question should be RMB 40,092,088. The specific calculation method is as follows: from December 15, 2009 to October 19, 2010 (the day before the rate adjustment) totaling 308 days, with an interest rate of 5.76%, the interest amount should be RMB 7,884,800 (RMB 40 million x 5.76% / 360 x 308 days x 4 = RMB 7,884,800); from October 20, 2010 to December 25, 2010 (the day before the rate adjustment) totaling 66 days, with an interest rate of 5.96%, the interest amount should be RMB 1,748,266.68 (RMB 40 million x 5.96% / 360 x 66 days x 4 = RMB 1,748,266.68); from December 26, 2010 to February 8, 2011 (the day before the rate adjustment) totaling 44 days, with an interest rate of 6.22%, the interest amount should be RMB 1,216,355.56 (RMB 40 million x 6.22% / 360 x 44 days x 4 = RMB 1,216,355.56); from February 9, 2011 to April 5, 2011 (the day before the rate adjustment) totaling 55 days, with an interest rate of 6.45%, the interest amount should be RMB 1,576,666.68 (RMB 40 million x 6.45% / 360 x 55 days x 4 = RMB 1,576,666.68); from April 6, 2011 to July 6, 2011 (the day before the rate adjustment) totaling 91 days, with an interest rate of 6.65%, the interest amount should be RMB 2,689,555.56 (RMB 40 million x 6.65% / 360 x 91 days = RMB 2,689,555.56); from July 7, 2011 to April 14, 2012 (the day before the start of the second stage interest under the Supplementary Agreement) totaling 282 days, with an interest rate of 6.90%, the interest amount should be RMB 8,648,000 (RMB 40 million x 6.90% / 360 x 282 days = RMB 8,648,000); from April 15, 2012 to September 14, 2012, totaling five months, calculated at the agreed rate of RMB 700,000 per month, the interest amount should be RMB 3.5 million; from September 15, 2012 to December 10, 2013 (the date of the first-instance judgment) totaling 451 days, with an interest rate of 6.40%, the interest amount should be RMB 12,828,444.44 (RMB 40 million x 6.40% / 360 x 451 days = RMB 12,828,444.44).

3. Whether the lawyer representation fees in question should be allowed. According to the Supplemental Agreement in question, Bei Hongfeng shall be liable for the payment of the lawyer representation fees incurred by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin in realizing their creditor's rights. Although Bei Hongfeng argued that such fees had not actually been incurred, the Entrusted Agency Agreement and Supplemental Agency Agreement between Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin, and Huacheng Law Firm explicitly stipulated the amount of lawyer representation fees, and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had already provided evidence of their remittance to Huacheng Law Firm, and the law firm also issued a receipt confirming receipt of the lawyer representation fees. Therefore, Bei Hongfeng's defense that the fees were not actually incurred and should not be borne by him cannot stand. As for the amount to be borne, since the Charging Guidance Standards provide a government-guided price standard for lawyer representation fees, Bei Hongfeng shall bear the liability for the corresponding lawyer representation fees based on such guided price standard, using the outstanding principal and interest owed by him to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin as the calculation base. According to the relevant provisions of the Charging Guidance Standards, for civil litigation cases where lawyer representation fees are charged as a percentage of the subject matter amount, the calculation method for the government-guided price is to charge the fee based on the amount of the disputed subject matter using a progressive rate method. In this case, as of December 10, 2013, the outstanding principal and interest owed by Bei Hongfeng to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin amounted to RMB 80,092,088 (RMB 40,000,000 principal + RMB 40,092,088 interest). Calculated according to the progressive rate method stipulated in the Charging Guidance Standards, the lawyer representation fee should be RMB 1,825,841.76 (calculation method as follows: 100,000 yuan x 10% + (1,000,000 yuan - 100,000 yuan) x 6% + (10,000,000 yuan - 1,000,000 yuan) x 4% + (80,092,088 yuan - 10,000,000 yuan) x 2% = RMB 1,825,841.76). The standard for charging lawyer representation fees agreed between Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin, and Huacheng Law Firm was higher than the aforementioned guided price standard, and its calculation base was also higher than the actual outstanding principal and interest amount owed by Bei Hongfeng. Therefore, the excess portion shall be borne by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin themselves.

4. Whether Donghao Company should assume the guarantee liability. Given that Donghao Company had, on April 14, 2012, convened an interim shareholders' meeting regarding the provision of guarantee for Bei Hongfeng and passed a resolution agreeing to provide the guarantee for Bei Hongfeng, among the three shareholders of Donghao Company, apart from Bei Hongfeng, Zhu Libing had signed the shareholders' meeting resolution, and Zhang Xicai, although not signing the resolution, had affixed his seal on the Supplemental Agreement agreeing that Donghao Company would provide the guarantee for Bei Hongfeng. That is, all three shareholders of the company agreed to provide the guarantee in question. According to the provisions of Article 16, Paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Company Law, which state: "Where a company provides a guarantee for a shareholder or actual controller of the company, it must be approved by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. The shareholders mentioned in the preceding paragraph or the shareholders controlled by the actual controller mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall not participate in the voting on the matters stipulated in the preceding paragraph. Such voting shall be passed by more than half of the voting rights held by other shareholders present at the meeting," the guarantee act in question is legal and valid, and Donghao Company shall assume joint and several guarantee liability for the loan in question. Furthermore, the guarantee scope stipulated in the Guaranteed Loan Contract and the Supplemental Agreement includes the lawyer representation fees paid by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin for realizing their creditor's rights. Therefore, Donghao Company shall also assume joint and several guarantee liability for this portion of the fees.

In summary, part of the claims of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin are established, and the court of first instance supported them accordingly. The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 200 and Article 206 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on the Trial of Loan Cases by People's Courts, and Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the Civil Judgment (2013) Hei Gao Shang Chu Zi No. 9: 1. Bei Hongfeng shall, within ten days of the effective date of the first-instance judgment, repay Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin the loan principal of RMB 40,000,000 and interest of RMB 40,092,208; 2. Bei Hongfeng shall, within ten days of the effective date of the first-instance judgment, pay Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin lawyer representation fees of RMB 1,825,841.76; 3. Donghao Company shall assume joint and several guarantee liability for the aforementioned debts; 4. Dismiss the other claims of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 591,800 shall be borne by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin in the amount of RMB 162,960, and by Bei Hongfeng in the amount of RMB 428,840; the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Bei Hongfeng.

Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. Change the interest amount of RMB 40,092,208 in item 1 of the first-instance judgment to RMB 27,263,628.22; 2. Revoke item 2 of the first-instance judgment and dismiss the claims of Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin regarding lawyer representation fees; 3. The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin. The main reasons are as follows:

First, the first-instance judgment's findings of fact are erroneous. Bei Hongfeng did not breach the contract, and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin were not entitled to sue for repayment before the performance period expired and to demand Donghao Company assume joint and several guarantee liability. The repayment period stipulated in the Supplemental Agreement was September 30, 2012, but Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit on July 9, 2012. The first-instance judgment's finding that Bei Hongfeng failed to provide statements and relevant materials to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin during the contract performance, constituting a breach, and that the conditions for early repayment as agreed by both parties were satisfied, are erroneous. First, the parties stipulated in the Guaranteed Loan Contract that "Party B has the right to inspect and supervise the use of funds, and Party A shall provide Party B with relevant statements and materials, etc." That is, the provision of statements and relevant materials by Party B is the result of Party A exercising its supervisory right; if Party A does not exercise its supervisory right, Party B does not need to provide such materials and statements. Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin never made such a request to Bei Hongfeng. Second, the parties did not specifically stipulate in the contract when and what materials and statements Bei Hongfeng should provide during the use of funds, which constitutes unclear stipulation on related matters. Moreover, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin never requested to view relevant materials and statements before the lawsuit. Under such circumstances, Bei Hongfeng's failure to provide materials and statements related to fund usage does not constitute a breach of contract. Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin's request for early repayment on this ground should not be supported.

Second, the first-instance court failed to re-conduct property preservation, which violated legal procedures. The first-instance court essentially ratified the unauthorized preservation actions and excessive sealing of assets by the Yichun Intermediate People's Court. The Yichun Intermediate People's Court, which initially accepted the lawsuit filed by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, had no jurisdiction, and all decisions and judgments made by that court in this case should be invalid. After the Heilongjiang High People's Court accepted the case, although Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company had provided relevant evidence proving the excessive sealing of assets by the Yichun Intermediate People's Court and requested the first-instance court to lift the excessive sealing of the houses, the request was not granted.

Third, Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company should not bear the interest incurred after Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit and applied for property preservation. Because Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company did not breach the contract, they should not bear any interest. Considering that the case has been under trial and exceeded the repayment date stipulated in the contract, they accept the outstanding principal and interest determined in the first-instance judgment up to July 16, 2012 (the date interest began to accrue). After July 16, 2012, because Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin prematurely filed the lawsuit and illegally preserved assets, Bei Hongfeng was unable to repay the debt on time. Therefore, the failure to repay on time was entirely caused by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, and Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company should not pay interest for this period.

Fourth, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin's claim for Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company to bear their lawyer representation fees should not be supported. The parties did not stipulate the amount or calculation standard for lawyer representation fees in the contract. Without providing the law firm's invoice, the first-instance court, based on the Beijing Lawyer Charging Guidance Standards, partially supported Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin's claims for lawyer fees, which has no legal basis.

Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin argued in defense that the first-instance judgment's findings of fact were clear and the application of law was basically correct. However, the judgment's calculation of interest only up to the date of the first-instance judgment was incorrect. Interest should be calculated up to the date of actual repayment.

The following facts were found in the second instance of this Court: On December 14, 2009, the Guaranteed Loan Contract signed by Bei Hongfeng as Party A and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin as Party B stipulated in Article 3, Paragraph 2: "Party B has the right to inspect and supervise the use of funds, and Party A shall provide Party B with relevant statements and materials, etc." Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the same contract stipulated: "In any of the following circumstances, Party B shall have the right to stop disbursing the loan and immediately recover the principal and interest of the loan already disbursed, up to the termination of this contract. (1) Party A and Party C provide false information including but not limited to statements and various materials. (2) Party A and Party C become involved in litigation with a third party, which may render them unable to repay the principal and interest to Party B..." Article 4, Paragraph 2 stipulated: "Party B has the right to inspect and supervise the use of funds, and Party A shall provide Party B with relevant statements and materials, etc."

During the second-instance trial of this Court, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin submitted the invoice for lawyer representation fees issued by Huacheng Law Firm in March 2014. The amount of the fee was RMB 1,825,841.76 as determined in the first-instance judgment.

Other facts found in the second instance of this Court are the same as those found by the first-instance court.

This Court holds that the main issues in dispute between the parties during the second instance are: 1. Whether Bei Hongfeng's conduct constituted a breach of contract. 2. Whether Bei Hongfeng should bear the interest incurred after Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit and applied for property preservation. 3. Whether Bei Hongfeng should pay the lawyer representation fees required by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin for realizing their creditor's rights. 4. Whether Donghao Company should assume joint and several guarantee liability.

(1) Regarding whether Bei Hongfeng's conduct constituted a breach of contract

This Court holds that the basis for determining whether Bei Hongfeng's conduct constituted a breach of contract is the provisions of the Guaranteed Loan Contract and its Supplemental Agreement signed by the parties. According to the Guaranteed Loan Contract, the loan period was from December 15, 2009 to June 15, 2010. According to the Supplemental Agreement, the loan period was extended to September 14, 2012. This is the basis for confirming the loan period and whether Bei Hongfeng repaid on time. However, Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the Guaranteed Loan Contract stipulated: "In any of the following circumstances, Party B shall have the right to stop disbursing the loan and immediately recover the principal and interest of the loan already disbursed, up to the termination of this contract. (1) Party A and Party C provide false information including but not limited to statements and various materials. (2) Party A and Party C become involved in litigation with a third party, which may render them unable to repay the principal and interest to Party B..." Article 4, Paragraph 2 stipulated: "Party B has the right to inspect and supervise the use of funds, and Party A shall provide Party B with relevant statements and materials, etc." In this case, the reason Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin demanded that Bei Hongfeng repay the loan and interest before the loan period expired was that Bei Hongfeng violated Articles 3, Paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Guaranteed Loan Contract and the relevant provisions of the Supplemental Agreement by refusing to provide statements and materials, information on the use of the loan, and had disputes with third parties, and even concealed assets from the lender and transferred assets at low prices to outsiders. However, in the first-instance trial, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin's allegations of Bei Hongfeng's breach mainly focused on his failure to provide relevant statements and materials. The issues of Bei Hongfeng's disputes with third parties, or his concealment of assets from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, or his low-price disposal of assets, were not addressed in the first-instance trial. Therefore, in this case, the question of whether Bei Hongfeng's conduct constituted a breach of contract focuses on whether he had the obligation to provide Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin with relevant materials and statements, when that obligation should have been performed, and whether Bei Hongfeng failed to perform that obligation. Through the first and second instance trials, it has been established that from the time Bei Hongfeng received the loan until the time Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit, he indeed did not provide any materials or statements to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin. The parties also never specifically agreed on the time, method, and conditions for providing materials and statements in the contract. Precisely because of this, the parties had differing understandings of the relevant content of the contract. This Court holds that the first-instance court's finding that Bei Hongfeng's failure to provide relevant statements and materials constituted a breach of contract, and that Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin therefore had the right to demand early repayment based on the contract, was correct. The defense by Bei Hongfeng that the contract only stipulated that the provision of false information including but not limited to statements and various materials by Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company constituted a breach, and that the failure to provide such materials was not explicitly defined as a breach, cannot stand. Article 125 of the Contract Law stipulates: "If there is a dispute between the parties over the understanding of a contract clause, the true meaning of the clause shall be determined in accordance with the words and expressions used in the contract, the relevant provisions of the contract, the purpose of the contract, transactional practices, and the principle of good faith." The contract signed by the parties was the Guaranteed Loan Contract. Specifically, the purpose of Article 4, Paragraph 1 of the contract is to ensure that the lender, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, have the right to know and supervise the use of funds, so that if they discover that Bei Hongfeng has changed the use of funds without authorization or other circumstances that may affect the lender's rights, they can take timely measures to recover the funds and interest. Applying the principle of teleological interpretation, it can be understood that while providing false materials and statements would certainly affect the lender's supervision of the borrower's use of funds, failing to provide relevant materials and statements would prevent the lender from understanding the use of the funds in question, hindering the timely exercise of their rights. Therefore, Bei Hongfeng's failure to provide relevant materials and statements to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin over the two-plus years of the loan constituted a breach of contract. According to the contract, under the circumstances of Bei Hongfeng's breach, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to demand early repayment and payment of interest.

(2) Regarding whether Bei Hongfeng should bear the interest incurred after Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit and applied for property preservation

This Court holds that, since Bei Hongfeng's conduct constituted a breach of contract, according to the contract, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to demand early repayment and payment of interest. In other words, under such circumstances, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin demanded that Bei Hongfeng repay the loan and pay interest early, and Bei Hongfeng was obliged to fulfill the obligation of repayment and interest payment based on the other party's request. As for the fact that Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin chose to assert their rights against Bei Hongfeng through litigation and applied for property preservation, this cannot become a reason to exempt Bei Hongfeng from his obligation under the contract to repay and pay interest. Therefore, Bei Hongfeng's appeal that he should not bear the loan interest after July 16, 2012, when Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin filed the lawsuit and applied for property preservation, cannot stand and is not supported by this Court.

(3) Regarding whether Bei Hongfeng should pay the lawyer representation fees required by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin for realizing their creditor's rights

This Court holds that Bei Hongfeng's appeal that he should not pay the lawyer representation fees required by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin for realizing their creditor's rights cannot stand. The reason is: Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin claimed lawyer fees from Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company based on the provision in the Guaranteed Loan Contract that the scope of guarantee liability assumed by Donghao Company "includes but is not limited to principal debt, interest (penalty interest), liquidated damages, litigation costs, travel expenses, lawyer fees, and all other expenses for realizing the creditor's rights." Although in the first instance, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin only provided the entrustment agency contract signed with Huacheng Law Firm and the receipt issued by that law firm, after the first-instance judgment was made, the law firm issued an invoice based on the amount of lawyer representation fees determined in the first-instance judgment. The act of the law firm assigning lawyers to appear in court and represent the clients objectively existed, and the invoice issued by Huacheng Law Firm proves that Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin indeed paid the lawyer representation fees for realizing their creditor's rights. Furthermore, when the first-instance court determined the amount of lawyer representation fees to be paid by Bei Hongfeng to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, it had already referred to the Beijing Lawyer Charging Guidance Standards and made an adjustment favorable to Bei Hongfeng regarding the agency fees stipulated in the entrustment agency contract between Li Zhanjiang, Zhu Limin, and Huacheng Law Firm. Given that Bei Hongfeng's breach of contract was the fundamental cause of the lawyer representation fees in question, this Court does not support Bei Hongfeng's appeal that he should not pay the lawyer representation fees to Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin.

(4) Regarding whether Donghao Company should assume joint and several guarantee liability

This Court holds that the first-instance judgment's finding that Donghao Company should assume joint and several guarantee liability for the debts borrowed by Bei Hongfeng from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin is not improper. First, although Bei Hongfeng borrowed money from Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin in his personal name, it can be seen from the provisions on the use of funds in the Guaranteed Loan Contract that the funds borrowed by Bei Hongfeng were precisely used for Donghao Company's "operation of the University Classic Project real estate development." Therefore, on April 14, 2012, Donghao Company convened an interim shareholders' meeting regarding the guarantee for Bei Hongfeng's loan and passed a resolution agreeing to provide the guarantee. Among the company's only three shareholders, apart from Bei Hongfeng himself, Zhu Libing signed the shareholders' meeting resolution, and the other shareholder, Zhang Xicai, affixed his seal on the Supplemental Agreement agreeing that Donghao Company would provide the guarantee for Bei Hongfeng. The above facts demonstrate that Donghao Company's act of providing a guarantee for Bei Hongfeng's loan complied with both the procedural requirements of the Company Law regarding a company providing a guarantee for a shareholder or actual controller and the actual needs of Donghao Company to develop the real estate project using the funds borrowed by Bei Hongfeng. Therefore, Donghao Company's argument that it should not assume guarantee liability cannot stand. As for Donghao Company's argument that the guarantee period began after the expiration of the performance period of the Guaranteed Loan Contract, and that Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin were not entitled to demand that Donghao Company also perform the guarantee obligation prematurely while demanding early repayment from Bei Hongfeng, this argument also cannot stand. Because the guarantor, Donghao Company, did not sign a separate guarantee contract with the creditor, Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin, but rather signed the Guaranteed Loan Contract and the Supplemental Agreement together with the debtor Bei Hongfeng and Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin. That is, Donghao Company was fully aware of the obligations of Bei Hongfeng stipulated in the Guaranteed Loan Contract, including the circumstances under which Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin had the right to demand early repayment from Bei Hongfeng. Under such circumstances, Donghao Company did not declare in the contract that it would refuse to assume joint and several guarantee liability when Bei Hongfeng was obligated to repay prematurely, so it shall be deemed to have accepted all the contents of the Guaranteed Loan Contract. Therefore, under the condition that Bei Hongfeng breached the contract and thus had the obligation to repay early, Donghao Company cannot be exempted from joint and several guarantee liability.

Bei Hongfeng also argued in the appeal that after Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin initiated the lawsuit, the Yichun Intermediate People's Court, upon their application, took preservation measures against the property of Bei Hongfeng and Donghao Company, and that the value of the preserved subject matter far exceeded the amount in dispute. However, after the case was transferred to the Heilongjiang High People's Court, that court did not issue a new preservation ruling or correct the excessive preservation by the Yichun Intermediate People's Court. This Court holds that if Bei Hongfeng believes he suffered losses due to the property preservation, he should file a separate lawsuit.

As for the issue raised by Li Zhanjiang and Zhu Limin during the trial at second instance that the first-instance judgment erred by setting the cut-off date for payment of interest by Bei Hongfeng as the effective date of the first-instance judgment and requesting the court of second instance to correct it and rule that the interest be paid up to the actual date of repayment, given that they did not file an appeal, this claim does not fall within the scope of the second instance of this case, and this Court will not entertain it.

In conclusion, this Court, pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, hereby renders the judgment as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment affirmed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee and property preservation fee shall be enforced in accordance with the first-instance judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 109,726.53 shall be borne by Bei Hongfeng and Shenyang Donghao Real Estate Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
